summary.text: All three companies flag macroeconomic and geopolitical exposure, but the specific risk architecture differs sharply by business model: Apple's Item 1A is organized around macroeconomic/industry, business, legal-regulatory and financial risks, with global supply chain concentration and majority-international sales as the core exposures (AAPL's FY2026 Q1 10-Q reports no material changes to these factors).

Apple's company-specific risks center on product transition execution, competition where it holds minority market share in smartphones, PCs, tablets and wearables, gross margin pressure from pricing, tariffs and FX, and reliance on a single product category for a significant portion of net sales.

Tesla's risks are dominated by execution and ramp risk in new products (driver assistance/autonomous systems, Cybercab Robotaxi, Bots, energy storage), demand uncertainty for electric vehicles, product defect and self-insured product liability exposure, and key-person dependence on Elon Musk.

Tesla is additionally distinctive in citing brand/credibility risk from third-party commentary and protests, and the risk that the 2025 CEO Performance Award product goals may be misaligned with consumer demand.

JPMorgan's principal risks are financial-institution categories with no direct analogue at the other two: legal and regulatory supervision, political, market, credit, liquidity, capital, operational, strategic, country and people risks, including credit-loss and private-credit contagion exposure and resolution-related creditor loss absorption.
Common ground across all three is cybersecurity and IT system failure, protection of personal information, and exposure to extraordinary events such as natural disasters, wars and health epidemics.

claims.text: Apple's FY2026 Q1 10-Q states there have been no material changes to its risk factors since the 2025 Form 10-K.
claims.quote: There have been no material changes to the Company's risk factors since the 2025 Form 10-K.

claims.text: Apple organizes its risk factors into Macroeconomic and Industry Risks, Business Risks, Legal and Regulatory Compliance Risks, and Financial Risks.
claims.quote: Macroeconomic and Industry Risks... Business Risks... Legal and Regulatory Compliance Risks... Financial Risks

claims.text: Apple says a majority of its total net sales are outside the U.S. and a majority of its supplier facilities, including manufacturing and assembly sites, are located outside the U.S., so performance depends significantly on global and regional economic conditions; adverse conditions include recession, inflation, higher interest rates and currency fluctuations.
claims.quote: the Company's global supply chain is large and complex and a majority of the Company's supplier facilities, including manufacturing and assembly sites, are located outside the U.S. As a result, the Company's operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions.

claims.text: Apple states it has a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer, tablet and wearables markets, and that failure to compete successfully can materially adversely affect its business.
claims.quote: The Company has a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer, tablet and wearables markets, and some of the markets in which the Company competes have from time to time experienced little to no growth or contracted overall.

claims.text: Apple identifies the need to successfully manage frequent introductions and transitions of products and services, including production ramp-up, inventory and third-party support risks.
claims.quote: To remain competitive and stimulate customer demand, the Company must successfully manage frequent introductions and transitions of products and services.

claims.text: Apple flags net sales and gross margin volatility from pricing pressure, competition, supply shortages, component costs, foreign exchange fluctuations, inflation, and new or increased tariffs and other trade restrictions.
claims.quote: fluctuations in foreign exchange rates; inflation and other macroeconomic pressures; the imposition of new or increased tariffs and other trade restrictions, their overall magnitude and duration, and retaliatory actions in response

claims.text: Apple notes it generates a significant portion of its net sales from a single product category and a decline in demand for that product could significantly impact net sales and gross margins.
claims.quote: the Company generates a significant portion of its net sales from a single product category and a decline in demand for that product could significantly impact net sales and gross margins.

claims.text: Tesla's lead risk is issues or delays in developing, launching and ramping production of products, services and features, with future business depending on driver assistance and autonomous driving solutions and increasing production of mass-market vehicles including Cybercab, its purpose-built Robotaxi product.
claims.quote: our future business depends on development of our driver assistance systems and autonomous driving solutions and increasing the production of mass-market vehicles, including Cybercab, our purpose-built Robotaxi product.

claims.text: Tesla also cites potential delays in launching and ramping Bots, energy storage products and Solar Roof, and AI-based products, and the need to advance AI capabilities and cost-effective manufacturing.
claims.quote: we are also developing Bots for future commercialization, and we may experience delays in launching and ramping the production of this product.We have experienced, and may also experience similar future delays in launching and/or ramping production of our energy storage products and Solar Roof

claims.text: Apple identifies information technology system failures and network disruptions, including ransomware and other cybersecurity incidents, and losses or unauthorized access to confidential and personal information as risks.
claims.quote: exposed to information technology system failures or network disruptions caused by natural disasters, accidents, power disruptions, telecommunications failures, acts of terrorism or war, computer viruses, physical or electronic break-ins, ransomware or other cybersecurity incidents

claims.text: Tesla notes electric vehicles still constitute a small percentage of overall vehicle sales and that demand for its vehicles could be affected by perceptions of range, charging access, competition, oil price volatility, government incentives and concerns about its future viability.
claims.quote: In addition, electric vehicles still constitute a small percentage of overall vehicle sales. As a result, the market for our vehicles could be negatively affected by numerous factors

claims.text: Tesla flags product defect, recall, warranty and product liability exposure, and states that in most jurisdictions it generally self-insures against product liability claims for vehicle exposure, meaning claims are paid from company funds rather than insurance.
claims.quote: In most jurisdictions, we generally self-insure against the risk of product liability claims for vehicle exposure, meaning that any product liability claims will likely have to be paid from company funds and not by insurance.

claims.text: Tesla cites key-person dependence, stating it is highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, its Chief Executive Officer, and that no key employee is bound by an employment agreement for a specific term.
claims.quote: we are highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, Technoking of Tesla and our Chief Executive Officer. None of our key employees is bound by an employment agreement for any specific term

claims.text: Tesla identifies brand and credibility risk from third-party commentary and criticism, which it says has incited protests, some escalating to violence targeting its operations, products and personnel.
claims.quote: Such attention can include criticism, which may be exaggerated or unfounded... and has incited protests, some escalating to violence targeting our operations, products and personnel.

claims.text: Tesla discloses a risk that the technologies and product goals associated with the 2025 CEO Performance Award may be misaligned with current or future consumer demand, causing it to miss better-aligned opportunities.
claims.quote: There is a risk that the technologies and initiatives associated with the 2025 CEO Performance Award, including the product goals, are misaligned with current or future consumer demand

claims.text: JPMorgan's principal risk factors are grouped as Legal and Regulatory, Political, Market, Credit, Liquidity, Capital, Operational, Strategic, Country and People risks.
claims.quote: The principal risk factors include:•Legal and Regulatory risks... •Political risks... •Market risks... •Credit risks... •Liquidity risks

claims.text: JPMorgan states its legal and regulatory risks include penalties from resolving litigation or investigations by governmental authorities, and losses that security holders and other unsecured creditors would absorb if the firm entered into a resolution.
claims.quote: the losses that security holders and other unsecured creditors will absorb if JPMorganChase were to enter into a resolution.

claims.text: JPMorgan says it can be vulnerable to competition from less regulated or unregulated firms, such as financial technology companies, and that larger firms like it often face more stringent supervision and regulation.
claims.quote: A highly-regulated financial services firm such as JPMorganChase can be vulnerable to competition from firms that are less regulated or unregulated.

claims.text: JPMorgan flags credit risk including that widespread consumer defaults could raise its allowance for credit losses and charge-offs, and that significant expansion of private credit could worsen losses among non-bank lenders and spread stress to broader funding and credit markets.
claims.quote: the interconnectivity across credit markets increases the risk that the significant expansion of private credit could worsen losses among non-bank lenders and their borrowers, particularly if stress or defaults spread to broader funding and credit markets.

claims.text: JPMorgan cites market risk from unfavorable economic and market events, interest rate and credit spread changes, and possible losses in its investment portfolio and market-making businesses that could reduce profitability, liquidity and capital levels.
claims.quote: Any significant losses in JPMorganChase's investment portfolio or from market-making activities could reduce its profitability and its liquidity and capital levels, and thereby constrain the growth of its businesses.

claims.text: JPMorgan cites operational risk including harm from a successful cyber attack or other extraordinary events, risks in safeguarding personal information, vendor oversight, data management, and its risk management framework and models.
claims.quote: the harm that could be caused by a successful cyber attack affecting JPMorganChase or by other extraordinary events

claims.text: Tesla cites security incidents affecting its data, products and service providers, noting its service providers, including its workforce management software provider, have been subject to ransomware and other security incidents.
claims.quote: Our service providers, including our workforce management software provider, have been subject to ransomware and other security incidents

claims.text: Tesla says its operations could be adversely affected by events outside its control such as natural disasters, wars, geopolitical conflicts and health epidemics, noting its Fremont Factory and Gigafactory Nevada are in seismically active regions and Gigafactory Shanghai is in a flood-prone area.
claims.quote: our Fremont Factory and Gigafactory Nevada are located in seismically active regions in Northern California and Nevada, and our Gigafactory Shanghai is located in a flood-prone area.

summary.text: NVIDIA's revenue scaled from $26.97 billion in FY2023 to $60.92 billion in FY2024 (up 126%) and $130.50 billion in FY2025, an unprecedented two-year expansion driven by Data Center.

Growth has continued into FY2026 but at a decelerating percentage rate: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $57.0 billion versus $35.1 billion a year earlier (+62%), and nine-month revenue was $147.8 billion versus $91.2 billion (+62%).

The underlying Data Center compute growth rate has stepped down sharply, from +217% in FY2024 and +133% year-on-year in Q3 FY2025 to +62% in H1 FY2026 and +59% for the first nine months of FY2026, while networking re-accelerated to +105% year-on-year in the FY2026 nine-month period.

The demand narrative has shifted from a supply-constrained Hopper ramp entering FY2025 to the Blackwell platform, which began production shipments in Q4 FY2025 and now drives both Compute & Networking and Graphics growth, with three platform shifts — accelerated computing, AI models and agentic applications — cited as drivers.

Margin and concentration signals have deteriorated alongside the growth: gross margin rose to 75.0% in FY2025 from 72.7% in FY2024 but fell to 72.4% in Q2 FY2026 (66.6% for H1 FY2026) after a $4.5 billion H20 inventory charge and a $4.0 billion sequential drop in H20 sales, and the largest direct customer grew from 13% of FY2024 revenue to 23% in Q2 FY2026.

summary.text: All five companies flag the same core regulatory exposures: extensive and increasing FDA/foreign approval and compliance requirements, government price controls and reimbursement pressure, and enforcement risk around marketing, pricing and promotional practices (JNJ C4/C9/C11, PFE C21/C25, MRK C40/C42, LLY C58/C59, ABBV C72/C73).

Pricing and access regulation is universal: JNJ, MRK, PFE and LLY all cite pervasive government involvement and price controls in the EU, Japan and China, while ABBV cites European government-mandated price reductions and Medicare/Medicaid-driven US pricing pressure.

Approval-timing and post-approval regulatory risk is also shared, including FDA budget/personnel reductions slowing reviews (JNJ), FDA-mandated post-marketing commitments that can cause label changes or loss of approval (PFE), heightened health-authority caution on benefit/risk (MRK), and safety findings in larger real-world populations (LLY, ABBV).

On mitigation, disclosure is thin and mostly qualitative: JNJ says it seeks to identify, manage and mitigate risks and relies on new products (about 25% of 2025 sales) plus a wholly owned captive insurer for product liability; PFE plans trials prudently; LLY announced preliminary voluntary pricing agreements with the U.S. government in November 2025 and monitors marketed-product safety; PFE monitors the EU HTA regulation rollout.

Company-specific regulatory pressure points differ: JNJ faces talc litigation and cGMP/recall exposure, LLY faces counterfeit and mass-compounded incretins plus BIOSECURE Act and tariff-driven supply constraints, MRK flags possible elimination of FDA user-fee programs delaying inspections and approvals, and ABBV and MRK highlight legislation encouraging faster generic/biosimilar approval.

claims.text: JNJ states it is subject to costly and complex U.S. and foreign laws and regulations, with FDA regulatory powers increasing required testing and documentation and the expense of product introduction.
claims.quote: The exercise of broad regulatory powers by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (the U.S. FDA) continues to result in increases in the amounts of testing and documentation required for U.S. FDA approval of new drugs and devices and a corresponding increase in the expense of product introduction.

claims.text: JNJ says changes to FDA timing or requirements for approval or clearance may negatively impact its ability to bring new products to market, and new laws may impose deadlines with insufficient time to comply.
claims.quote: For example, changes to the U.S. FDA's timing or requirements for approval or clearance of our products may have a negative impact on our ability to bring new products to market.

claims.text: JNJ states rapid increases in new government laws and regulations impose significant compliance costs, and cGMP compliance issues can lead to fines, recalls, shortages, delays in new product approvals and litigation.
claims.quote: Regulatory issues regarding compliance with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) (and comparable quality regulations in foreign countries) by manufacturers of drugs and devices can lead to fines and penalties, product recalls, product shortages, interruptions in production, delays in new product approvals and litigation.

claims.text: PFE states the U.S. healthcare industry is highly regulated and subject to frequent and substantial changes, and that federal or state legislative or regulatory action could adversely affect its business.
claims.quote: The U.S. healthcare industry is highly regulated and subject to frequent and substantial changes. Any significant additional efforts at the U.S. federal or state levels to reform the healthcare system by changing the way healthcare is provided or funded could have a material impact on us.

claims.text: PFE discloses it has received inquiries, subpoenas and information demands from government authorities and has incurred significant expense, civil payments and fines from such claims and actions.
claims.quote: Like many companies in our industry, we have from time to time received, and may receive in the future, inquiries and subpoenas and other types of information demands from government authorities.

claims.text: MRK states its research, preclinical testing, clinical trials, manufacturing and marketing are subject to extensive regulation by the FDA and foreign authorities including in the EU, Japan and China, and that its products cannot be marketed without obtaining and maintaining regulatory approval.
claims.quote: The Company's activities, including research, preclinical testing, clinical trials and the manufacturing and marketing of its products, are subject to extensive regulation by numerous federal, state and local governmental authorities in the U.S., including the FDA, and by foreign regulatory authorities, including in the EU, Japan and China.

claims.text: LLY states that marketing, promotional and pricing practices are subject to extensive scrutiny and regulation, and that investigations and claims can bring criminal charges, fines, penalties and exclusion from U.S. healthcare programs.
claims.quote: Such investigations, litigation, and claims result in substantial expense and other significant consequences, including in some cases criminal charges and fines, criminal and civil penalties, damages, and other monetary or non-monetary remedies, including exclusion from U.S. federal and other healthcare programs.

claims.text: ABBV states its products are subject to rigorous regulation by numerous authorities and that obtaining approvals can be costly and time consuming, with approvals possibly not granted on a timely basis, if at all.
claims.quote: The process of obtaining regulatory approvals to market a pharmaceutical product can be costly and time consuming, and approvals may not be granted for future products, or additional indications or uses of existing products, on a timely basis, if at all.

claims.text: JNJ states that outside the U.S., major markets including the EU, UK, Japan and China have pervasive government involvement in healthcare funding and impose price controls or limit access and reimbursement.
claims.quote: Outside the U.S., numerous major markets, including the EU, United Kingdom, Japan and China, have pervasive government involvement in funding healthcare and, in that regard, directly or indirectly impose price controls, limit access to, or reimbursement for, the Company's products, or reduce the value of its intellectual property protection.

claims.text: MRK states that in the EU, Japan and China governments fix pricing and reimbursement, that Japan mandates annual price reductions, and that it expects pricing pressures to continue.
claims.quote: In Japan, the pharmaceutical industry is subject to government-mandated annual price reductions of pharmaceutical products and certain vaccines... The Company expects pricing pressures to continue in the future.

claims.text: PFE states that in markets such as EU member states, the U.K., Japan, China, Canada, Australia and New Zealand governments have significant power as large single payors to regulate prices and impose cost control, citing China's QCE and VBP tender process causing significant price cuts.
claims.quote: For example, the QCE and VBP tender process in China has resulted in significant price cuts for off-patent medicines.

claims.text: ABBV states many European countries have ongoing government-mandated price reductions and that U.S. Medicare and Medicaid laws and managed care practices contribute to pricing pressures.
claims.quote: In particular, many European countries have ongoing government-mandated price reductions for many pharmaceutical products, and AbbVie anticipates continuing pricing pressures in Europe.

claims.text: JNJ states development and regulatory approval of new products may be delayed due to limits on federal agency budgets or personnel, including reductions to the FDA's budget, employees and operations.
claims.quote: Moreover, the development and regulatory approval of new products may be delayed due to limits on federal agency budgets or personnel, including reductions to the U.S. FDA's budget, employees, and operations, which may lead to slower response times and longer review periods.

claims.text: PFE states the FDA may require post-marketing commitments such as additional clinical trials, results of which have in the past impacted its products and could result in loss of marketing approval or labeling changes.
claims.quote: The results generated in these trials have in the past impacted certain of our products and could impact our products in the future, such as by resulting in the loss of marketing approval, changes in labeling, and/or new or increased concerns about safety and/or efficacy, including newly discovered adverse events.

claims.text: MRK states health authorities such as the FDA, EMA, Japan's PMDA and China's NMPA have increased their focus on safety when assessing benefit/risk and appear more cautious about approvability of new products or indications.
claims.quote: health authorities such as the FDA, the EMA, Japan's PMDA and China's NMPA have increased their focus on safety when assessing the benefit/risk balance of drugs. Some health authorities appear to have become more cautious when making decisions about approvability of new products or indications.

claims.text: LLY states products are approved based on controlled trials of fixed duration, and after launch broader use may lead to identifying new or expanded safety or efficacy concerns.
claims.quote: After approval and launch, the products are used for longer periods of time by much larger numbers of patients, which may lead to identifying new or expanded safety or efficacy concerns.

claims.text: ABBV states that if new safety or efficacy issues arise or governments change standards, it may amend conditions of use, and sales could be halted by AbbVie or by regulatory authorities.
claims.quote: If safety or efficacy issues with an AbbVie product arise, sales of the product could be halted by AbbVie or by regulatory authorities and regulatory action could be taken by such regulatory authorities.

claims.text: JNJ states it seeks to identify, manage and mitigate risks to its business, though many risks are outside its control and cannot be eliminated.
claims.quote: The Company seeks to identify, manage and mitigate risks to our business, but uncertainties and risks are difficult to predict and many are outside of the Company's control and cannot therefore be eliminated.

claims.text: JNJ reports that new products introduced within the past five years accounted for approximately 25% of 2025 sales, offsetting revenue losses from competition and loss of exclusivity.
claims.quote: New products introduced within the past five years accounted for approximately 25% of 2025 sales.

claims.text: JNJ states it does not purchase third-party product liability insurance but utilizes a wholly owned captive insurance company subject to certain limits.
claims.quote: The Company does not purchase third-party product liability insurance; however, the Company utilizes a wholly owned captive insurance company subject to certain limits.

claims.text: PFE states it tries to plan clinical trials prudently and to reasonably anticipate and address challenges, with no assurance of an optimal balance.
claims.quote: We try to plan clinical trials prudently and to reasonably anticipate and address challenges, but there is no assurance that an optimal balance between trial conduct, speed and desired outcome will be achieved.

claims.text: PFE states that with the EU Health Technology Assessment Regulation taking effect in January 2025, it is engaging and monitoring application of the EU's new clinical assessment program.
claims.quote: In addition, with the European Regulation on Health Technology Assessment (EU HTA-R) taking effect in January 2025, we are engaging and monitoring application of the EU's new clinical assessment program to new oncology products and certain biologic products submitted to the EMA.

claims.text: LLY announced in November 2025 preliminary voluntary agreements with the U.S. government to lower Medicaid and certain other drug prices and to launch new medicines with a more balanced pricing approach across developed nations.
claims.quote: In November 2025, we announced preliminary voluntary agreements with the U.S. government in which, among other arrangements, we agreed to implement measures to lower Medicaid and certain other drug prices for U.S. patients and to launch new medicines with a more balanced pricing approach across developed nations.

claims.text: JNJ is a defendant in numerous lawsuits arising out of the use of body powders containing talc, and could be required to pay significant amounts in settlements or judgments, potentially in excess of accruals.
claims.quote: For example, the Company is a defendant in numerous lawsuits arising out of the use of body powders containing talc, primarily JOHNSON'S Baby Powder.

claims.text: LLY states it continues to see production, marketing and sale of counterfeit, misbranded, adulterated and mass-compounded incretins in the U.S. and other markets, and that its actions to stop illegal sales are costly and may be ineffective.
claims.quote: we continue to see the production, marketing, and sale of counterfeit, misbranded, adulterated, and mass-compounded incretins in the U.S. and other markets that could materially impact us... Our actions intended to stop or prevent illegal sales of such medicines are costly and may be ineffective.

claims.text: LLY cites U.S. legislation intended to limit supply chain reliance on China, including the BIOSECURE Act, and 2025 U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods, as potential sources of supply disruption and higher costs.
claims.quote: U.S. officials have enacted and continue to consider legislation or other actions that are intended to limit supply chain reliance on China, including the BIOSECURE Act... In 2025, the U.S. government imposed new tariffs on Chinese goods and China responded with tariffs on select U.S. goods.

claims.text: MRK states that if the FDA drug user fee programs were eliminated, that could cause significant delays to facility inspections and approvals of new products.
claims.quote: Additionally, if the FDA drug user fee programs were eliminated, that could cause significant delays to facility inspections and approvals of new products.

claims.text: ABBV states proposals emerge from time to time for legislation to further encourage early and rapid approval of generic drugs or biosimilars, which if enacted could increase the impact of generic or biosimilar competition.
claims.quote: In addition, proposals emerge from time to time for legislation to further encourage the early and rapid approval of generic drugs or biosimilars. Any such proposals that are enacted into law could increase the impact of generic or biosimilar competition.

claims.text: LLY states health authority guidelines and legislative actions could make it less burdensome for biosimilar competitors to enter the market, which could have a material adverse effect on its business.
claims.quote: Particularly for biosimilars, health authority guidelines and legislative actions could continue to make it less burdensome for competitor products to enter the market and further incentivize uptake of biosimilars.

claims.text: MRK states it is subject to a variety of U.S. and international laws and regulations, including additional health care reform initiatives with mandatory discounts or fees, and that compliance costs or non-compliance could adversely affect its business.
claims.quote: The costs of compliance with such laws and regulations, or the negative results of non-compliance, could adversely affect the business, cash flows, results of operations, financial condition and prospects of the Company

summary.text: At September 30, 2025 JPMorgan reported a Standardized CET1 ratio of 14.8% (Advanced 14.9%) on $287,297 million of CET1 capital, versus Bank of America's Standardized CET1 ratio of 11.6% on $202.9 billion of CET1 capital.

The two CET1 ratios sit against different regulatory minimums — 12.3% Standardized for JPM versus 10.7% Standardized for BAC for the period ended September 30, 2025 — so headroom, not the level, is the comparable measure.

Third-quarter 2025 net interest income was $23,966 million for JPMorgan (up 2% year over year) against $15,233 million for Bank of America (versus $13,967 million in Q3 2024), both in USD millions for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

On uninsured deposits, JPMorgan disclosed Firmwide estimated uninsured deposits of $1,548.1 billion at September 30, 2025, while the only Bank of America figure in the excerpts is from its FY2024 10-K — estimated uninsured U.S. deposits of $646.2 billion and non-U.S. deposits of $124.9 billion at December 31, 2024 — a different date and a split rather than firmwide presentation.
BAC's MD&A net interest income includes FTE adjustments of $154 million in Q3 2025, so its managed-basis discussion is not on the identical basis as JPM's reported NII.

summary.text: Bank of America's FY2024 10-K organizes its material risk factors into categories including Market, Credit, Geopolitical, Business Operations (including cybersecurity), Regulatory/Compliance and Legal, Reputational, and Other (competition, models, data, climate).

Market risk stems from economic, political, social and health conditions, interest rate and currency movements, equity/commodity/futures price volatility, credit spreads and funding costs, with potential liquidity shortfalls and impacts on the liquidity coverage ratio.

Credit risk arises from macroeconomic stress, leveraged borrowers, elevated interest rates and cost of living, sector stress (notably commercial real estate office), and concentrations by industry, geography, product, asset class or counterparty — including heavy concentration in the financial services industry and clearing-member exposure.

Geopolitical risk covers doing business worldwide including emerging markets, exposure to sanctions, capital controls, currency moves and widening regional or military conflicts, alongside extensive and less predictable non-U.S. laws, rules and regulations covering bribery, AML and sanctions.

Operational risks include failure or breach of its own or third parties' operations and information systems, cybersecurity incidents and security breaches which it expects to continue with increased frequency and severity, employee misconduct or error, and reliance on models and data management.

Other named risks are the potential ineffectiveness of the risk management framework across the seven key risk types, significant legal and regulatory liability from lawsuits and government action, reputational harm, intense competition from bank, nonbank and new entrants, and climate/low-carbon transition risk.

claims.text: Market risk drivers cited include the level and volatility of interest rates, inflation, supply chain disruptions, employment levels, home prices, commercial property values, bank failures and liquidity concerns, trade policies, and digital asset volatility.

claims.text: Liquidity and cost of funds may be impacted by reputation risk, investor confidence, debt market disruption and credit spreads, with potential increased costs, a liquidity shortfall and/or impact on the liquidity coverage ratio.

claims.quote: Increased market volatility and adverse changes in financial or capital market conditions may increase our market risk.Our liquidity, competitive position, business, results of operations and financial condition are affected by market risks such as changes in interest and currency exchange rates, fluctuations in equity, commodity and futures prices

claims.text: Credit risk can be magnified by lending to leveraged borrowers and declining asset prices; a recessionary environment or rising unemployment could impair borrowers, and certain sectors such as commercial real estate, particularly office, remain at risk.

Certain sectors also remain at risk (e.g., commercial real estate,
particularly office) as a result of shifts in demand and tight financial and credit conditions.

claims.text: Concentrations of credit risk may reside in a particular industry, geography, product, asset class or counterparty, and BAC has significant credit concentrations with the financial services industry, plus clearing-member exposure to client non-performance.

claims.text: Under Geopolitical risks, BAC is subject to numerous political, economic, market, reputational, operational, compliance, legal, regulatory and other risks in the jurisdictions where it operates, including emerging markets.

claims.text: Widening regional conflicts or military conflicts elsewhere could cause economic disruptions, financial market volatility, higher inflation and asset valuation changes that disrupt operations.

claims.quote: We also rely on our employees, representatives and third parties in our day-to-day operations, who may, due to illness, unavailability, the emergence of widespread health emergencies or pandemics, human error, misconduct ... cause disruptions to our organization and expose us to operational losses, regulatory risk and reputational harm.

summary.text: NVIDIA reports two operating segments — Compute & Networking (Data Center accelerated computing/AI, networking, automotive, Jetson, DGX Cloud) and Graphics (GeForce gaming, GeForce NOW, Quadro/RTX workstation, vGPU, automotive infotainment, Omniverse) — with the CEO as CODM assessing segment revenue and operating income.
In Q3 FY2026 Compute & Networking generated $50,908 million of revenue versus $6,098 million for Graphics, out of $57,006 million total, i.e. roughly 89% of revenue from Compute & Networking.

For the first nine months of FY2026, segment revenue was $131,828 million for Compute & Networking and $15,983 million for Graphics ($147,811 million total), up from $80,157 million and $11,009 million a year earlier.

For full fiscal 2025, Compute & Networking revenue was $116,193 million and Graphics $14,304 million of $130,497 million consolidated, with segment operating income of $82,875 million and $5,085 million and an unallocated "All Other" operating loss of $(6,507) million.

NVIDIA supplements segment data with a revenue-by-end-market disclosure — Data Center (split into Compute and Networking), Gaming, Professional Visualization, Automotive, and OEM and Other — where Q3 FY2026 Data Center was $51,215 million of $57,006 million total, and a geographic split by customer headquarters location.
